purpose: Meropenem is a powerful antibiotic used to fight serious bacterial infections in the hospital, such as infections of the lungs, belly, skin, urinary tract, and brain. It is often used when other antibiotics have not worked or when the infection is severe. It is given by a nurse through an IV (into your vein), not taken by mouth.
how_it_works: Meropenem works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Without this protective wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. It targets a very wide range of harmful bacteria, which is why doctors reach for it when infections are tough to treat.
common_side_effects: You may experience nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, headache, or rash. The area where the IV goes in may become sore or inflamed. Some people get a mild rash or itching during the infusion.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin, other antibiotics, or any medications, because there is a small chance of a serious allergic reaction. Rarely, meropenem can cause seizures, especially in people with kidney problems or a history of seizures. Taking antibiotics can sometimes cause a severe type of diarrhea called C. difficile — let your doctor know right away if you get bad diarrhea during or after treatment. Your doctor will likely monitor your kidney function while you are on this medicine.
typical_dosing: Meropenem is given through an IV by a nurse or doctor, usually every 8 hours (three times a day). The exact dose depends on the type and severity of your infection, your weight, and how well your kidneys are working. Treatment usually lasts 5 to 14 days depending on your infection.
